newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia UBK says mulls merger in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia UBK says mulls merger in 1997.

text.p: Slovenian bank UBK said on Thursday it was mulling a merger with a larger domestic bank and said the link-up was likely to happen in the second half of the current year.

"It is very possible that the merger will happen in the second half of this year but it is too early to say which bank will be involved," Vlasta Grjol, UBK's executive director of global finances, told Reuters.
UBK, with a domestic market share of less than 0.9 percent, is one of 28 banks operating in Slovenia's overcrowded financial sector.
The bank has been considering a merger since the end of last year when it started negotiations to link up with competitor Gorenjska banka, so far without any results.
UBK said it was in talks with several banks and that Gorenjska banka was one of them.
Analysts have predicted a wave of bank mergers in Slovenia this year as the pressure to cut costs and prepare for future foreign competition mounts.
In January, bank Noricum merged with bank Celje, while Dolenjska bank also said recently it was considering a merger this year but declined to give any further details.

Slovenia's parliament is expected to pass a law this year enabling foreign banks to establish full branches in Slovenia in line with European Union legislation. At the moment, international banks can only open subsidiaries, requiring substantial capital outlays. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
